chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, all together, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade Al-Nitaaf and Al-Arba'.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Arba' is that a dam is built, so water is held back and the land is irrigated with it, then one becomes independent of it.'
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not sell it, but lend it to your neighbor.'
And Al-Nitaaf is that one has the right to drink (from a source), so he becomes independent of it, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not sell it, but lend it to your brother or your neighbor.'

key_terms.أَعِرْهُ: Lend it (gratuitously); to give for temporary use without charge.
key_terms.الشِّرْب: The right to drink or use water from a specific source.
key_terms.النِّطَاف: Water rights or shares; specifically having a portion of water that one can use or dispose of.
key_terms.الْأَرْبَعَاء: A dam or barrier built to hold back water for irrigation purposes.
key_terms.جَارَكَ: Your neighbor; referring to those living in proximity with whom one shares resources.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Al-Arba' and Al-Nitaaf in Islamic water jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi distinguishes between Al-Arba' (impounding water via a dam) and Al-Nitaaf (holding a specific water share), establishing that ownership does not automatically confer the right to sell for profit. The Prophet’s instruction to 'lend' rather than 'sell' reflects the Shia juristic principle of preventing hoarding and ensuring equitable access, prioritizing communal welfare over commercial exploitation in resource management.
